ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle JKL. Point R is on side JK; the two segments of side JK have the same three pink tick marks, indicating that R is the midpoint of JK; point S is on side KL, and the two segments have the same one tick mark, indicating that S is the midpoint of KL; point T is on side JL, and the two segments have the same two tick marks, indicating that T is the midpoint of JL. Segments LR, JS, and KT are all drawn and intersect at interior point P. Reasoning: Because R, S, and T are respectively the midpoints of the three sides of the triangle, LR, JS, and KT are the three medians of the triangle, and their point of intersection P is the centroid. The centroid divides each median in the ratio from vertex to centroid : centroid to midpoint = 2:1. On segment LR, L is the vertex and R is the midpoint, so LP:PR = 2:1. Given RP = 3.5, therefore PL = 2 × 3.5 = 7. JP = 9 does not need to be used to find PL.
